sentences.text: Social worker Priya Nair conducted a needs assessment visit on Monday following a referral from the hospital after Margaret Doyle's discharge.
Margaret Doyle lives in a home with heating that she feels is too cold for the current season.
Margaret Doyle has an 11-year-old cat named Biscuit who is the only other pet in the house.
Margaret Doyle identified her GP as Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery on Church Lane, noting Dr Patel retired last summer.
Margaret Doyle stated she has not been referred to a falls clinic or service, though she noted there might be a pile of letters.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated that the current house is too difficult for Margaret Doyle (S2) due to the stairs and garden.
Kevin Doyle (S3) expressed that Margaret Doyle (S2) would be better off in a sheltered flat or a bungalow with a warden on site.
Margaret Doyle (S2) denied moving to a sheltered flat or bungalow, stating she has not moved since coming here as a bride.
Margaret Doyle (S2) recalled Frank carrying her over a step when she was a bride.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she does not want to go to a flat with strangers.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she would not sell the house because she would not know where her dog 'Biscuit' would go or where Frank's roses would go.
Margaret Doyle reported that her grandson, Jordan (Susan's son, age 22), has been borrowing her bank card to withdraw cash or make purchases.
Margaret Doyle stated that her bank statements showed withdrawals totaling approximately six hundred pounds over the last two months, which she attributed to Jordan.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that she gave Jordan her bank card number and PIN when she first came out of hospital so he could get her shopping.
Margaret Doyle stated that Jordan still has her bank card and said he would bring it back on Saturday.
Kevin Doyle stated that his mother (Margaret) did not tell him about the withdrawals because of 'that face' (implying his reaction to the news).
Kevin Doyle reported that his mother gave Jordan her PIN when she came out of hospital so he could do her shopping.
Social worker Priya Nair thanked Margaret Doyle for being honest with her during the assessment.
Social worker Priya Nair thanked Kevin Doyle for bringing tea.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not trust herself to carry two cups of tea and a walking frame through the house.
Margaret Doyle described a fall on the third of March (Monday) in the kitchen while attempting to make tea.
Margaret Doyle was uncertain whether she tripped or felt dizzy, stating she honestly did not know.
Margaret Doyle reported she was on the floor for approximately two hours until Brenda (a neighbour) found her.
Brenda, a neighbour with a key, found Margaret Doyle by noticing her curtains were not drawn and the kitchen light was off.
Brenda called an ambulance and sat on the floor holding Margaret Doyle's hand until the ambulance arrived.
Margaret Doyle stated she could not call anyone herself during the fall because her phone was in the front room and she could not reach it.
Margaret Doyle reported she did not bang her head when she fell, despite being asked repeatedly at the hospital.
Margaret Doyle stated she might have felt a bit woozy before the fall because she had not eaten much that day.
Margaret Doyle was admitted to St Aldhelm's hospital on the orthopaedic ward for four days.
Margaret Doyle reported she had broken her left wrist, which she identified as her good hand as she is left-handed.
Margaret Doyle reported she had no hip fractures, only bruising on the side of her body.
Margaret Doyle's wrist cast was removed last Tuesday, and she is now wearing a splint that she must wear most of the time.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not do enough wrist exercises.
Margaret Doyle uses a walking frame indoors most of the time, which she hates but relies on.
Margaret Doyle sometimes holds onto furniture instead of using the walking frame indoors because the frame gets caught on rugs and doorframes.
Margaret Doyle has only been out of the house to the end of the path and to the doctor's since returning home.
Margaret Doyle expressed uncertainty about her ability to manage daily tasks due to her left wrist fracture, noting difficulties with opening jars and doing buttons.
Margaret Doyle stated she could previously walk to the shops (approx. 10 minutes), get her paper, and walk back slowly, but now feels frightened of going out again.
Margaret Doyle reported three falls in the last six months: one in the garden before Christmas, one in January in the bathroom where she caught herself on the sink, and one on the
Margaret Doyle described her home environment as having stairs leading to a bedroom and a bathroom/toilet located upstairs.
Margaret Doyle explained she tries not to drink too much in the afternoons to avoid needing to use the toilet frequently.
Margaret Doyle described using the stairs by holding onto a rail on the right side when going up, and going down sideways or sometimes sitting on her bottom when tired because the
Margaret Doyle stated she uses only one bathroom frame, leaving it at the bottom of the stairs and holding onto the wall upstairs.
Margaret Doyle mentioned there are several rugs in the hall and elsewhere, some belonging to her late husband Frank's mother and one brought from a holiday in Wales.
Margaret Doyle stated she gets up to use the toilet once or twice a night and currently leaves the landing light on.
Margaret Doyle reported she has not had a proper bath since January (before the fall in January), only managing a strip wash at the sink.
Margaret Doyle stated Brenda washed her hair over the kitchen sink last week, but she does not want to keep asking her to do it.
Margaret Doyle described dressing as very slow (40 minutes to an hour), taking a long time to get buttons and bra hooks undone, and wearing the same cardigan most days because it
Margaret Doyle stated she has given up wearing tights and now wears elasticated trousers, and can put on slippers but not shoes with laces.
Margaret Doyle reported she sometimes does not get dressed in the morning (wearing only a nightie) on some days, citing that 'nobody's coming' as a reason.
Margaret Doyle stated she is not wearing a pendant alarm or any neck device, though her son Kevin mentioned such items.
Margaret Doyle stated she sometimes does not get dressed in the morning, wearing only a nightie, on some days.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that she sometimes cannot make it to the toilet in time, resulting in a bit of leaking, particularly when rushing up the stairs.
Margaret Doyle stated she wears pads at night and buys them from the supermarket.
Margaret Doyle reported that Kevin buys the pads for her at the big shop, though she is unsure what he thinks about this.
Margaret Doyle expressed interest in seeing the continence service if it is free.
Margaret Doyle stated she is happy to be referred to the continence service and asked the social worker not to make a big thing of it.
Margaret Doyle described her evening meal as a yoghurt, and sometimes crackers and cheese if she can be bothered cutting the cheese.
Margaret Doyle stated it is hard to cut the cheese with one hand.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she has not turned the cooker on since she came home after the fall.
Margaret Doyle stated she cannot lift the pans and admitted she does not like being in the kitchen because that is where the fall happened.
Margaret Doyle reported her clothes are hanging off her and she lost nearly a stone since Christmas.
Margaret Doyle stated her current weight is eight stone something, having been nine and a half stone for her married life.
Margaret Doyle reported her appetite comes and goes and she does not feel hungry like she used to.
Kevin Doyle is responsible for doing a big shop on Sundays when he comes to visit.
Brenda gets Margaret milk and bread in the week if she runs out.
Margaret Doyle stated she has a microwave and uses it to make a jacket potato sometimes.
Margaret Doyle reported Kevin put ready meals in the freezer, but she cannot get the film off the top.
Margaret Doyle stated she sometimes has trouble opening the blister pack flaps for her medication and uses a butter knife.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she missed her blood pressure tablet (amlodipine) twice last week (Tuesday and Thursday mornings).
Margaret Doyle attributed the missed medication to being distracted since the fall.
Margaret Doyle stated she takes amlodipine (5mg once daily in the morning) and alendronic acid (70mg once a week on Monday).
Margaret Doyle stated she takes paracetamol for her wrist (up to four times a day) but only takes it once or twice a day if it is aching.
Kevin Doyle (S3) reported that the back step into the garden is a big drop.
Kevin Doyle (S3) reported that the light at the top of the stairs is on a pull cord, which Margaret Doyle (S2) has to reach round for.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated the house is warm enough generally.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he persuaded Margaret Doyle (S2) to get a new boiler last year, noting it took him three months.
The social worker summarised that since falls on the third of March and two prior falls, Margaret is finding it very hard to wash properly (bathing and hair), getting dressed takes
The social worker summarised that getting dressed takes up to an hour and wears Margaret out.
The social worker summarised that Margaret is not able to prepare proper meals, is eating very little, and has lost nearly a stone.
The social worker summarised that Margaret has missed some tablets.
The social worker summarised that Margaret is on her own a lot, feels lonely, and is feeling more low than usual.
The social worker stated that the above impacts have a significant effect on Margaret's wellbeing, physical health, safety, mood, and ability to see people.
The social worker stated that it is likely Margaret will meet eligibility criteria for support, but this must be agreed.
Margaret Doyle stated she would not be put into a care home as a result of this assessment.
Margaret Doyle stated she is happy for the social worker to share information with her GP and anyone involved in her support.
Margaret Doyle expressed a strong wish to have a bath again and feel properly clean, noting she cannot do her hair with one hand.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish for a second rail on the stairs and a second frame upstairs to improve safety.
Margaret Doyle stated she would like to have a bath lift, noting her late husband Frank's sister had one.
Margaret Doyle stated she is interested in the assessment and has no objection to it.
Margaret Doyle stated she is an 'old woman' but does not want to look like one.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated that the house matters to her because it is her home, where she brought up the kids, and she knows every creak in the house.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she wants to stay in her own home for as long as she possibly can.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she would want to go to Beechwood if she ever had to go into a home, noting Brenda's sister was there and they were lovely.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she is not yet ready to go into a home, saying she is not there 'by a long chalk'.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he is not trying to shove Margaret Doyle (S2) out of the house, but he worries.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish that Kevin would be told about the withdrawals, stating, 'He'll have to know, won't he. He'll be the one sorting it out.'
Margaret Doyle stated that staying in her own home with her dog 'Biscuit' is the most important thing for her.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish to be able to have a proper bath and wash her hair.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish to return to the lunch club to see Joan and Pat.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish to stop being frightened of falling and the kitchen.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish to be able to cook a proper dinner occasionally (e.g., mince and potatoes).
Kevin Doyle mentioned Margaret's roses and Frank's roses.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish to see the roses bloom this summer and be well enough to go out and look at them.
Margaret Doyle admitted she did not tell her GP about the two earlier falls (the garden and January incidents), though her son Kevin knows about the garden fall because he found 'm
Kevin Doyle stated that Brenda (a neighbor) told him a few weeks ago that she thought she saw Jordan at a cash machine on the high street by the chemist with a card, but noted that
Kevin Doyle reported that Brenda was unsure it was Jordan because she does not wear her glasses half the time.
Kevin Doyle stated that he heard from one of Jordan's old mates' mothers that Jordan has gotten himself into debt with betting apps on his phone.
The social worker (Priya Nair) recorded Kevin's report about the betting debt as 'something that's been said to you, not as something we know.'
Kevin Doyle stated that he thought they should ring the police because the situation sounds like theft.
Margaret Doyle stated she did not want the police involved and said, 'I'm not having the police round here for Jordan. I'm not.'
Margaret Doyle stated her wishes are for Jordan to stop using her card and for her to get her card back.
The social worker (Priya Nair) explained that she has a duty to take the report seriously as a safeguarding concern because it sounds like someone may be taking money without her (
The social worker (Priya Nair) explained that the safeguarding team would look at what happened and what would help keep Margaret safe, noting that Margaret's wish for Jordan to be
The social worker (Priya Nair) stated that the police would only be involved if Margaret decided she wanted them or if there was a risk to someone else.
Kevin Doyle stated that he still thought Jordan wanted to get a 'clip round the ear' (physical punishment).
Margaret Doyle's son, Kevin Doyle, is on an early shift and may visit the house around half eleven.
Margaret Doyle stated Kevin usually contributes money ('tuppence') to the household expenses.
Margaret Doyle stated she manages her own money for bills and cash out, though she admitted she has been a bit short lately and is not sure where the money is going.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she is short of money and unsure where it is going.
Kevin Doyle stated he came straight from work and smells of the warehouse.
Margaret Doyle confirmed she is happy for Kevin to join the rest of the assessment.
Kevin Doyle stated he has been telling Margaret about the rugs for years.
Margaret Doyle stated she has been thinking about the rugs since about 2010.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he is able to come over mainly on Sundays to do the big shop and sit with Margaret Doyle (S2), sometimes midweek if he is on early shifts.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he lives in Northampton, which is a forty-minute car journey, and works shifts at a warehouse.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he has two teenagers and his wife works, limiting his availability.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated her daughter Susan lives in Spain (Alicante) and moved there with her husband eight years ago.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Susan rings every week on Sunday nights and comes over in the summer.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated Susan was on the phone to him every day when Margaret Doyle (S2) had the fall.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Susan was worried sick when she had the fall.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Brenda (next door) pops in most days, just for a minute.
Margaret Doyle (S2) described a routine where Brenda knocks on the wall in the morning and Margaret knocks back so Brenda knows she is alright.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Brenda is seventy-six years old and has knee problems, so she cannot lean on her too much.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she used to attend the lunch club at St Michael's church hall every Wednesday.
Margaret Doyle (S2) described the lunch club as a proper dinner with a cooked meal, pudding, and activities like bingo, a quiz, or a talk.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated there was a man with real owls in a box at the lunch club, and one sat on her arm.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated Margaret Doyle (S2) talked about the owl for a month.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she had not been to the lunch club since the fall.
Margaret Doyle identified the bank as Midshire (a building society) where her pension goes.
Margaret Doyle has a state pension and receives half of Frank Doyle's railway pension as a widow.
Margaret Doyle and Frank Doyle own the house, which was paid off years ago.
Margaret Doyle has approximately £9,000 in savings at a building society, which she describes as funeral money and a bit for grandchildren.
Margaret Doyle denied receiving Attendance Allowance, stating she did not know what it was.
The social worker explained that Attendance Allowance is for people over state pension age needing help with personal care, is not means-tested, and Margaret might be entitled to.
Kevin Doyle offered to help Margaret fill in the Attendance Allowance form due to her hand difficulties.
The social worker explained that a financial assessment may be required if the council arranges ongoing care, depending on income and savings, but the house is not counted.
Margaret Doyle expressed a preference to pay a contribution to stay in her home rather than move elsewhere.
Kevin Doyle agreed to take Margaret to the Midshire branch on Friday morning to cancel the card and order a new one.
The social worker (Priya Nair) agreed to refer the case to the safeguarding adults team and contact Margaret.
The social worker proposed a request for reablement, described as short-term (usually up to six weeks), free, and involving carers to help Margaret regain confidence and do things
The social worker proposed a request for reablement involving morning visits for washing, dressing, and tablets, and teatime visits for meals.
The social worker proposed reablement visits starting every day, tapering off as Margaret gains confidence.
The social worker stated that the reablement request is not yet agreed, requires manager approval, and an outcome will be provided by the end of next week.
The social worker stated that Margaret does not want carers to be bossy in her kitchen.
The social worker confirmed she would refer Margaret to occupational therapy today for a bath lift/board, second stair rail, second upstairs frame, and assessment of the back step.
The social worker stated the occupational therapy waiting list is approximately three weeks and she would mark the referral as a priority due to falls.
The social worker stated she would make a safeguarding referral about the card this afternoon.
Kevin Doyle agreed to see the social worker again on the fifteenth.
Kevin Doyle instructed the social worker to see the person again on the fifteenth.
